text:
jess (product): Hey folks — I dropped a PRD draft for the Reserved GPU SLA + autoscale behavior. Link: https://redwood.internal/prd/reserved-gpu-sla-rfc

jess (product): Asks: confirm SLA targets, per-GPU throughput assumptions, autoscale cooldowns, and acceptance criteria for launch. Especially worried about surge handling and fallback.

ravi (eng): Skimming now. Can we list current throughput assumptions? e.g., tokens/s per A100/RTX... Also need to define what 'surge' means (x2 sustained vs x10 spiky).

maria (eng-ml): For our latest quantized LLMs, baseline is ~1200 tokens/s per A100 for gen workloads at 1024 context. Re-ranking and embeddings differ. I'll add a table in the doc.

sam (sre): We need SLOs on 99p latency and cold-start time. Proposal: 99p gen token latency < 150ms, cold-start < 6s for new model instance, autoscale cooldown 60s, max scale rate +25%/min.

jess (product): Good. Add acceptance criteria: 1) 99p latency met under committed load for 30d; 2) failover to lower-tier model on capacity loss within 5s; 3) canary rollout <1% impact.

ravi (eng): Edge cases: partial GPU OOM causing degraded throughput, KV cache warmup for chat state causing first-request spikes, and model rollback path. I'll sketch required instrumentation (per-route token counters, instance health signals).

maria (eng-ml): Also call out quantization regression checks: fidelity drop beyond 2% P95 perplexity triggers rollback. We'll wire that into Redwood Optimize as an eval hook.

nina (sales): From enterprise customers: they want hard SLA credits for dedicated pools and a runbook for incident notification. Can marketing + legal template be attached?

deploy-bot: New PRD uploaded by jess. Link: https://redwood.internal/prd/reserved-gpu-sla-rfc (sha: a1b2c3)

jess (product): Next steps: @ravi and @sam to add specific metrics and instrumentation by EOD Thursday. @maria to add model throughput table. After that, we'll cycle the RFC to eng-privacy and sales for final input. :thumbsup:

ravi (eng): Will do. Quick question — do we set an explicit burst capacity policy for <1min spikes? I vote yes: allow transient burst up to 3x committed for 30s with throttling fallback.

sam (sre): Agreed but must be bounded. Suggest burst credit bucket per customer, documented in PRD.

jess (product): OK let's capture that. I'll update PRD with those items and ping the thread when ready for final review.
